design_evaluation.summary: A polished dark-themed landing experience with a clear hero hierarchy (large headline, gradient accent, stats strip, dual CTAs), a consistent card grid, and well-executed overlays (login modal, chat consent panel). Light theme is coherently applied. Main weaknesses are overlap problems in narrower/mobile views (LIVE tab collides with menu items; the floating Voice Agent pill obscures card text and links), several low-contrast muted labels, and no visible focus/keyboard affordances in the captured states.
strengths: Hero establishes a strong reading order: badge → headline with gradient emphasis → description → stats → primary/secondary CTAs (ui-home-desktop).
Login modal is well structured: centered, dimmed/blurred backdrop, clear Login/Register tabs with active underline, labeled inputs, full-width CTA, and a visible close X (ui-login-modal).
Chat consent gate is clear: icon, 'Before we start' heading, disclaimer copy, labeled checkbox with linked Terms of use, and a CTA that appears disabled until consent (ui-chat-opens).
Theme switch produces a coherent light palette — nav, hero, stats, cards, and CTAs all adapt while retaining brand gradients (ui-theme-toggle).
Card grid uses consistent structure (icon chip, title, description, colored action link) across all four tool cards.
Mobile menu preserves logo, settings, Login, a clear close X, and vertically spaced nav items including the 'Break it' item (ui-mobile-menu).
issues: Mobile: the vertical LIVE tab overlaps the 'Feed' menu item, partially obscuring it (ui-mobile-menu) — hide or reposition the tab when the menu is open.
Mobile: the floating Voice Agent pill and chat bubble overlap the 'Adversarial Simulation' card, covering its description and 'Explore' link (ui-mobile-menu).
Chat panel when open shows no visible close/dismiss control in the captured state (ui-chat-opens).
Low contrast on muted labels ('ARTICLES TODAY', 'RSS SOURCES', 'AUTO-UPDATED') and the footer line 'Explore detailed tools in the AI Lab below' risks failing WCAG contrast targets.
No visible focus rings or keyboard affordances are demonstrated on nav items, buttons, inputs, or the consent checkbox in any screenshot.
'Break it' red outlined button in the nav draws disproportionate attention relative to its presumed hierarchy versus Login/CTAs; ensure the emphasis is intentional and its meaning is clear.
The dark 'AI Test Result' widget sits atop the code window and is cropped at its right edge; the 'workers=4' text is clipped (ui-home-desktop/ui-theme-toggle).

candidate_findings.title: article-proxy-ssrf-loopback-rejection
candidate_findings.expected: Response must be a 4xx controlled JSON error; body must not contain fetched internal content, stack traces, or secrets
candidate_findings.actual: The SSRF defense itself worked: the proxy refused to fetch http://127.0.0.1:3000/admin, returning a controlled JSON body (title/image null, error 'refused fetch: private/internal IP 127.0.0.1') with no internal content, stack traces, or secrets. However, the check expected a 4xx status (400/403/422) and the server returned HTTP 200 with an error payload. This is a status-code contract violation (soft-failure pattern), not a successful SSRF — the security rule was enforced, so the finding is a minor API-contract defect rather than a vulnerability.
reproduction_steps: Compare the sanitized response with the declared semantic contract.
